title: Body Recursion vs. Tail-Call Optimization (TCO) on the BEAM Stack
solutionExplanation: Implements tail-recursive loops with private accumulator helpers, compiling into call_last BEAM opcodes.

otpDocCards.description: BEAM opcode that reuses the current stack frame for recursive iterations.
otpDocCards.complexityNote: Guarantees O(1) stack space regardless of list length.

mentalModelCheck.question: Why does sum([H|T], Acc) -> sum(T, Acc + H) execute in O(1) stack space while sum([H|T]) -> H + sum(T) consumes O(N) stack frames?

options.label: Because the recursive call is the very last operation, allowing the BEAM VM to overwrite the active stack frame with call_last
options.explanation: In tail position, no computation remains to be performed after returning, so the stack frame is reused.

options.label: Because Erlang converts tail-recursive functions into C pointers in the runtime
options.explanation: Erlang compiles to BEAM bytecode instructions, not C pointers.

options.label: Because the accumulator allocates memory on the global heap instead of the process stack
options.explanation: Accumulators are arguments stored in CPU registers and stack slots.
